newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Small blast in Arab Jerusalem, five slightly hurt.
newsitem.headline: Small blast in Arab Jerusalem, five slightly hurt.

text.p: A small bomb exploded at an Israeli Interior Ministry office in Arab East Jerusalem on Thursday, injuring five people slightly and causing light damage, police and medical officials said.
Israel's first aid service, Magen David Adom, said five people were slightly injured in their ears by concussion from the blast.
Police said damage was caused to a door of the office. They closed the street in front of the site and began searches.
A police spokesman told Reuters it was not known if the attack had a criminal or nationalist background.
Israeli radio stations said police were investigating all motives, criminal and nationalist, including the possibility a Jewish militant might have planted the bomb at the office.
Palestinians use the Interior Ministry in East Jerusalem to obtain documents required by Israeli authorities.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and soon after annexed it, a move not recognised by the international community.

Israel has been on high security alert since Sunday when security sources said there was information a guerrilla squad was in Israel to avenge the October 26, 1995, assassination in Malta of Islamic Jihad leader Fathi Shqaqi. His killers were not captured. Palestinians blamed Israel.
The alert has focused on areas frequented by Israelis. The Jewish state fears another suicide attack like a series of four over nine days in February and March that killed 59 people in Israel.

Those attacks were claimed by the Hamas movement, which along with Islamic Jihad, has led violent opposition to interim peace deals between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel by attacking the Jewish state.
